critical_errors.issue: The cited XiaBook Proposition 6.2.5 states continuity of the maximum operation under d_S convergence; it does not state closure of the P-preorder under simultaneous d_S limits. The required closure result is Proposition 6.2.4, so the cited theorem does not support the deduction.
Schneider's Theorem 4.1.8 is not the John ellipsoid theorem and therefore does not support the normalization B^n subseteq L_j S_j+b_j subseteq nB^n.

The cited XiaBook Remark 10.3.1 body-resolution formula is equation (10.21), not equation (10.22). Equation (10.22) concerns changing the smooth reference metric and does not imply Delta_nu(L_i,h_i)=Delta_nu(A_i)+nu(D_i).

gaps.issue: The monotonicity implication (55.30) is delegated entirely to eq:ok-i-order of thm:ok-algebraic-volume-order, but that internal result is not present among the supplied premises or dependency edges.

The essential valuation-independent diagonal formula lambda_n(Delta_nu(theta,u))=vol(theta,u)/n! is invoked without proof or a declared premise statement. It supplies both the volume-gap convergence and the uniform positive lower bound.

The assertions that the I-envelope is I-equivalent to the original potential, preserves every partial body, is a model potential, and satisfies the mass-volume identity rely on unavailable internal results thm:complex-i-projection, I-invariance of partial bodies, and eq:complex-mass-volume.

The specialization from partial bodies of metrics with minimal singularities to ordinary Okounkov bodies relies on the unavailable internal theorem thm:ok-algebraic-volume-order, so this deduction cannot be checked from the declared context.
